newsitem.title: UK: Palladium price sinks on word Russia may export.
newsitem.headline: Palladium price sinks on word Russia may export.

text.p: The price of palladium dropped $6.00 from early trading levels on Thursday to $154.00 per ounce after news Russia may soon sign a delayed decree to resume exports.
The head of the Russian finance ministry's precious metals department said supply of palladium group metals (PGMs) that also include platinum to Japan could resume in May.

Palladium had risen by 40 percent from a low of $114.25 late last November because of delays in talks between Russia, the largest supplier, and leading importer Japan to negotiate sale contracts for 1997.

The rare white metal, used in electronics and dental alloys, was fixed at a fresh 21-month high of $160.25 in London on Thursday morning, up $3.25 from Wednesday's fix, then it fell on the news from Moscow.
Vladimir Rybkin said in a telephone interview in Moscow: "I think that the decree may be signed next week. I think it is possible that there will be deliveries in May."
Platinum was dragged lower by palladium and indicated at $366.50/$367.50, down about $2.50 from early dealings.
